svg.title: The four alignment levels of business architecture as rising steps, with the trigger that places a scenario and the deliverable each level demands
svg.desc: Four steps rise from left to right. Technology specific, a domain-specific architecture, triggers on one domain and a product decision and delivers product comparisons and selection advice. Technology architecture, a multi-domain architecture, triggers when two or more domains must work together and delivers a cross-domain integration design. Business solutions, partial business architecture, triggers when ROI, TCO or CAPEX enter the discussion and delivers a business case and decision matrix. Business transformation, business-led architecture, triggers on a new market or a digital strategy and delivers a roadmap and evolution plan. Design freedom widens as the level rises, and a note at the bottom gives the reading test for placing a scenario.
svg.text: The business asks for more with every level, and the design budget grows with it
Level 1 buys a product; level 4 may legitimately overturn the architecture you already have
trigger: one domain, a product call
the business is buying an outcome
and asking whether it was worth it

so last year's design is evidence,
only this level may overturn the
The reading test: see ROI / TCO / CAPEX and the scenario sits at level 3 · see “enter a new market” or “digital strategy” and it sits at level 4.
Answering a level 4 need with a level 1 report is the level mismatch in the pitfalls table; the reverse is the same error.
Level and depth are decided before the design starts, because they set how much process the project can carry.
